Reading 100 bytes out of a userspace wrapper through `fgets()` made a HUNDRED
`stream_read()` calls. php makes six: it reads a chunk and keeps what the line
does not need, and that buffer survives the call — so the whole file is consumed
in `ceil(100/17)` reads however many `fgets()` calls walk it. The leftovers go
into the same per-stream holding area a refused `stream_get_line()` uses, which
is php's stream read buffer, so `fread()` sees them too.
